➢ How do I read this sheet?

7
Team Compositions

8
➢ Teams are simply arranged based on Trekker release order.
➢ The first Trekker listed in each team composition is always considered the Main Slot Trekker.
➢ The second Trekker is usually the primary Support Slot Trekker.
➢ The remaining Trekkers are candidates for the final Support Slot, listed in order of their effectiveness for the team.
➢ Trekkers with universal buff effect will not be included unless they offer exceptional value as an alternative option. This is done to reduce the clutter with how much team compositions there are.

*Exception:
- Some team compositions require both Support Slot Trekkers as mandatory picks. In these cases, only the last listed Trekker is flexible and may be swapped out if they are needed for another team.

9
Main Discs

10
Main Disc priorities are determined by overall team utility with these specific Crescendo criteria in mind:

• C1 for Limited, Standard, and Finale Echoing Discs
• C6 for Cataclysm and Event Discs

About Support Discs
You will usually choose Discs that provide the highest relevant stat for the team. Of course, it is best if it also matches the note requirements of your Main Discs but only think of this when we have more Disc options.

Typically, the stats you are looking for are:
• Base ATK
• Elemental DMG%
• AA/Skill DMG%

11
Emblems

12
➢ All emblem affixes are based on the highest rarity.
➢ Emblem affixes with GREEN background indicate that they are the best emblem affix to go for in that slot.
➢ Affixes are ordered by priority from most important (top) to least important (bottom).
➢ Having an Elemental PEN stat of any rarity for your DPS is always better than having none, but do not lock PEN below Gold or Rainbow rarity.

13
Potentials

14
➢ The recommendations are based on maxed out Monolith Research and Ascension Difficulty 8.
➢ All Potentials are arranged based on acquisition and level upgrade priority.
➢ Level 1: Safe to not upgrade past the base level
➢ Level 1+: Upgrade the Potential as much as you can if possible
➢ Level 6: Always upgrade the Potential to its maximum level

*For specific questions, go to the #help-and-advice channel of Stella Sora Official server.

31

Minova's role in this team is to provide Lux DMG Taken debuffs with her More Than Just Pretty potential.

★ Key Notes:
• Space out Minova's Main Skill usage by only using each phase after every AA5 hit so More Than Just Pretty's uptime is constantly active.

• Both Ashwind Rhythm and Light Burn are treated as QoL potentials in this case because they are only taken for their unique effects and not for the Skill DMG buff that they provide. | Minova is relegated as a supporter for Firefly on this team so it's best to not upgrade any of her skills.

Currently in testing phase.

Firefly's Giant Sword build relies heavily on Auto Attack DMG. This is currently her best solo DPS build because none of the current units have Lucent mark trigger (except Firefly herself on Main slot).

★ Key Notes:
• Radiance Blade: Blazing Edge requires a full Lux team to function.
• Luminous Onslaught requires consistent Mark triggers to stack its effects, which Minova cannot do so it is not included in this build.

Starflare Pursuit (Support Skill) is the only important skill to max out as this is Firefly's prominent source of damage. Additionally, both Radiance Blade: Blazing Edge and Radiance Blade: Pursuing Slash's DMG output scale with its level.

Shia (5★) | 10/10/1/1+ (Auto Attack > Main Skill >> Ultimate)

72

Shia's Snow Rabbit build involves taking advantage of the Auto Attack chain reset mechanic by doing Dodge → Hold (until you see Snow Rabbit drones behind her) → Auto Attack repeatedly.

★ Key Notes:
• Hare's Pursuit is a very good potential that will allow you to spam the dash cancel technique even faster than without it, allowing for more dash cancels in a given period of time.
• If you dash cancel precisely after Shia uses her Main Skill, you can skip the delay in her skill's cooldown.
• Sticking as close as possible to the enemy is the name of the game. The goal is to shotgun the enemy at point blank to make sure that all of the bullets hit.

Sail of Twin Moons (Auto Attack) will be the main priority as most of Shia's damage output lies on it, especially with the dash cancel tech.

73

Phantom Step Radiance and Rimecrystal Edge scales based on the level of Whirling Waves (Main Skill).

74

Using Divine Deluge (Ultimate) usually results in a slight DPS loss since it is much better to just spam Shia's AA1, leading to it being entirely ignored or used in situations where you need the i-frame it provides while still dealing damage.

89

*Currently in re-evaluation phase.

Tilia is the premier must-have support for Lux teams as she provides Lux DMG Taken debuffs plus ATK% and Mark DMG% buffs along with a consistent Lux Mark application.

★ Key Notes:
• Blinding Beam becomes an optional potential if: 1) you can speedrun the boss faster than 16s which makes it so that the accumulated DMG overtime of Lux Mark triggers are negligible and 2) you can't keep the boss within Holy Inscription's circle due to its mobility.
• Perfect Spiral is preferred as not only does it provide a Skill DMG Taken debuff but also because the cooldown reduction from Renewed Spectrum is somewhat redundant due to her buffs having a near 100% uptime.

Future Relevant Notes (WIP):
• According to ZiLenTz's testing (it's timestamped), Trick Boost refreshes its duration when Tilia leaves the field for some reason. This means that it actually has better uptime and has perfect synergy with Renewed Spectrum.

Aegis Intervention (Support Skill) provides an ATK% buff to the team when her skill deals DMG. This buff scales according to the level of the skill and thus, it is beneficial to upgrade it.

Shia (5★) | 10/10/1/10 (Auto Attack > Main Skill >= Ultimate)

141

Just as the Snow Rabbit build is recognized as the best boss-fighting composition, the Night Rabbit build is similarly regarded as one of the strongest AoE builds in the game.

★ Key Notes:
• This build deals quadratic damage when enemies are clumped up.
• Wave to Oblivion is important to have if you plan on using her Ultimate against singular tanky enemies.
• Some Snow Rabbit potentials (Glacial Dash and Subzero Dominion) are decent to have since her attack pattern still scrolls through the AA1-AA4 sequence.
• Leporine Gale is taken in situations where you are able to group up enemies from a distance in order to be able to take advantage of its effects.

Sail of Twin Moons (Auto Attack) will be the main priority to level for this build. Moonlight Overflow scales based on its skill level.

142

Astral Pirouette scales based on the level of this skill.

143

Divine Deluge (Ultimate) helps with dealing against tanky enemies. Due to the nature of this build being strictly good against AOE, sudden singular tanky enemies becomes a pain to deal without using Ult.

Jinglin (4★) | 1/1/1/1 (Not needed)

242

For a 4-star Trekker, Jinglin has an innately high Mark DMG multiplier. This is further amplified primarily through her own potentials as well as Tilia's Blinding Beam.

★ Key Notes:
• This team is primarily used in AoE content like Menace Arena.
• if you want to use it against single target bosses, Jinglin has to dash after every skill cast to prevent wasting all 4 stacks in one go because Mark triggers have a 1s internal cooldown.
• Conductor Conversion is the most important potential to take in order to amplify her Mark DMG output.
• Leakage Protection allows her Ultimate to also trigger Marks, with its scaling being the same as her Main Skill's Mark DMG.
• Lord of Beasts is only taken for its ATK interval reduction effect to stack Auspicious Spirit faster. | As none of her skills affect her Mark DMG, it is not recommended to level up any of them.
